title: Writing HCL for our modules
bridge: Reading an HCL module is like reading a React component. Variables are props, outputs are what it returns, and for_each is a map() that renders one resource per item. Except changing a key in that map is not a re-render. It destroys one real resource and creates another.
intro: Three modules hold the sandbox infrastructure: aws-vpc-private (the network), aws-sandbox-pool (launch templates and warm pools) and aws-egress-proxy (Squid). This lesson reads them with the HCL features they use. Then it changes one safely and checks it with fmt, validate and a plan.

picture.caption: One sizes map flows through the pool module: a template and a group per key, and outputs keyed the same way.

steps.text: passes sizes = { lite, full, wide } and warm_pool_size
each group points at the template with the same key
IDs and names go out as maps keyed by size
you run fmt, validate and a plan before the PR

p: Start reading a module at variables.tf: it is the module's props. Each variable has a type, and can have a validation that fails the plan with your message.
aws-sandbox-pool (G3-11, G3-15) takes a name prefix, the sizes map, the warm pool size per size, the subnets and the tags. The validation keeps warm pools within the group's max_size of 3.
sections.because: We validate inputs in the module so a wrong number fails at plan time with a clear message, not in AWS.

notes.text: Types are checked before anything runs: string, number, bool, list(...), map(...), object({...}).
A description shows up in docs and error messages. Write it for the next reader.
alltrue over a for expression: every value between 0 and 3.
The message the person sees when the plan fails. Say what is allowed.

p: G3-11's launch templates are one resource block with for_each = var.sizes. OpenTofu makes one template per key. Inside the block, each.key is the size and each.value is the instance type.
Other resources are referenced by type.name.attribute. Below, the template points at the instance profile and the security group. Part 2 points at the KMS key. All three live elsewhere in the module.
sections.because: We use for_each over the sizes map because one block keeps all three sizes under identical rules.

notes.text: One template per key: aws_launch_template.sandbox["lite"], ["full"], ["wide"].
${...} inside a string: ai-agents-sandbox-lite and so on.
each.value is the map's value for this key: the instance type.
A nested block written on one line. The profile is another resource in this module.
The metadata rules from p3-3, now in HCL. Note the snake_case names.

p: Some settings are nested blocks, not arguments, and a block cannot take a list. A dynamic block writes one block per item. Inside content, the iterator is named after the block: tag_specifications.value.
merge() combines maps, and later maps win. The account's tags come first, then the two tags the sweeper and the claim code rely on.
sections.because: We generate the tag blocks because the instance and its volume need the same tags, and a copy-pasted block drifts.

notes.text: References the module's own KMS key. Its key policy must allow the AutoScaling role (p3-3).
The ticket asks you to check this argument exists in the pinned provider. validate will tell you.
dynamic "<block name>": one tag_specifications block per item of for_each.
The iterator is named after the block. Here it is "instance", then "volume".
each.key still refers to the outer for_each: the size.

sections.h: The group: reference by the same key
p: G3-15's groups use the same for_each. aws_launch_template.sandbox[each.key] picks the template with the same key, so lite's group always launches lite's template.
var.warm_pool_size[each.key] reads a map by key. If the map lacks a key that sizes has, the plan fails with an error. That is what you want: a missing pool size is a mistake.
sections.because: We key everything by size because then a size is added or removed in one map, and every piece follows.

notes.text: The sandbox subnets from the vpc unit, through a dependency (p4-2).
Same key, so each group launches its own size's template.
$Latest: a template change applies to the next VM without touching the group.
A map read by key. lite and full get 2, wide gets 0 to start.
The finish-setup hook from p3-4: 30 minutes, then ABANDON.

p: An ASG takes tags as repeated tag blocks, each with propagate_at_launch, so VMs from the group get them too. A dynamic block over a merged map writes them.
Outputs return values to whoever calls the module. Here, maps keyed by size, written with for expressions over the resources. Other units read them through a dependency.
sections.because: We propagate the tags at launch because the sweeper finds warm VMs by ai-agents:managed and the ASG's own tag.

notes.text: for_each over a map: the iterator's key and value are the tag's key and value.
Copy this tag onto every VM the group launches.
A for expression that builds a map: { lite = "lt-...", full = "lt-...", ... }.
The claim code (G3-18) finds groups by name: ai-agents-sandbox-<size>.

p: aws-vpc-private (G3-03) wraps the registry module terraform-aws-modules/vpc/aws at version 6.5.1. Its inputs are what p3-2 built by hand: private_subnets from cidrsubnet, public_subnets = [], create_igw = false, enable_nat_gateway = false. Its own resources add the S3 endpoint with the bucket policy, written with jsonencode().

aws-egress-proxy (G3-09) is the one place with a way out. It cuts two /28s from the spare fourth /18 and adds an internet gateway. A route table sends 0.0.0.0/0 to it, and squid.conf comes from a template. Below is a sketch of those parts; p4-5 covers Squid itself.
sections.because: We build the config file with templatefile() because the allowed source ranges come from Terraform, not from a hand-edited file.

notes.text: The same expression you ran in tofu console in p3-2.
templatefile() fills ${sandbox_cidrs} in the .tpl file. The result goes into the proxy VMs' user data, the script a VM runs at first boot.
count makes N copies, numbered by count.index. for_each is better when items have names.
Associate this table with the two proxy subnets only (aws_route_table_association, not shown).
The one route the sandbox subnets never get. G3-12 decides between this and Squid on inf.

p: Before a PR, run what CI runs: tofu fmt -check and terragrunt hcl format --check. Then tofu validate, which checks types and references with no cloud access. Then a plan, read line by line.

Renaming is the classic trap. Rename a resource label or a for_each key and the plan destroys the old resource and creates a new one. A moved block tells OpenTofu that the old address is the new one, so the plan has no changes. If the key is also part of a name, such as ai-agents-sandbox-${each.key}, the name changes and the resource is replaced anyway.
sections.because: We write a moved block whenever an address changes, because without it a rename destroys real VMs and groups.

code.file: a module change, before the PR
code.text:
tofu fmt -check -recursive            # what terrugrunt-lint.yml runs
terragrunt hcl format --check         # the same for terragrunt.hcl files
tofu init -backend=false && tofu validate
# renamed aws_launch_template.sandbox to .this? Add this, then plan shows no changes:
# moved {
#   from = aws_launch_template.sandbox
#   to   = aws_launch_template.this
# }

notes.text: Exit code 3 and a list of files when formatting is off. Fix with tofu fmt.
-backend=false: no state, no credentials. G7-17 runs exactly this in CI for every module.
moved covers every instance of a for_each resource at once.

sections.ifInstead: If instead validate says 'Unsupported argument' for volume_initialization_rate, the pinned provider does not support it. That is the check G3-11 asks for: remove the line and say so in the PR.

sections.h: Pointing the AWS provider at moto
p: For the lab we want real provider checks with no real AWS. The provider block below uses fake keys, skips the account lookups, and sends every call to moto. A plan of new resources makes no API calls, so moto only matters if someone runs apply by mistake.
The aws provider is a large download, a few hundred MB, the first time you run init.
sections.because: We send the provider to moto so that even a mistaken apply in the lab stays on your laptop.

notes.text: Same pin as the repo, so validate checks against the same schema DevOps uses.
Fake keys. Never put real keys in a .tf file.
Do not call STS to check the keys or to find the account ID.
Every service this module uses goes to moto.

quiz.q: You rename the for_each key "wide" to "big" in sizes. What does the plan do to wide's launch template and group?

options.text: Updates them in place with the new key
options.why: A for_each key is part of the address; a new address is a new resource.

options.text: Destroys and recreates them. A moved block fixes the addresses, but the names contain the key, so they are replaced anyway
options.why: name = "...-${each.key}" changes too, and a launch template's name cannot change in place.

options.text: Nothing, because the instance type did not change
options.why: The address and the name both changed.

options.text: The current item of the dynamic block's for_each: "instance", then "volume"
options.why: The iterator is named after the block.
That is each.key, from the resource's own for_each.
The tags are an argument inside content; the iterator walks the list.

quiz.q: Why does the pool module validate warm_pool_size?

options.text: Because AWS rejects any warm pool over 2
options.why: AWS allows larger pools. The limit is our max_size of 3.

options.text: So the PR reviewer does not have to read the plan
options.why: Validation catches one mistake early; reading the plan stays a person's job.

options.text: So a wrong number fails at plan time with a clear message instead of at apply time in AWS
options.why: Errors are cheapest before anything runs.

words.plain: A module input with a type and an optional validation; the module's props.
A value a module returns; other units read it through a dependency.
Makes one copy of a resource per map key or set item; each.key and each.value inside.
Writes one nested block per item, with an iterator named after the block.
Combines maps into one; later maps win on the same key.
Fills a template file with values and returns the text, like squid.conf.
Tells OpenTofu an old address is now a new one, so a rename is not a destroy.

tickets.why: The launch templates: for_each over sizes, metadata rules, an encrypted disk and a dynamic tag block.
The groups: the same keys, warm_pool from a map, the finish-setup hook, and Spot groups.
aws-vpc-private wraps the registry VPC module and adds an S3 endpoint policy with jsonencode().
aws-egress-proxy: two /28s, the only internet route, and squid.conf from templatefile().

remember: Read a module from its variables, follow the keys through for_each, and before any PR run fmt, validate and a plan. A rename needs a moved block.
